Predecessor of the AB models (replaced 2019); the manual read is for the 1600AB Plus. Thermistor readouts are an AB feature, so no readout is assumed here. Manufacturer maximum roast times run up to 25:30 (1 lb, profile P5); defaults 8:30 / 12:00 / 18:00 for 1/4, 1/2, 1 lb; Full City+ roasts: reduce to 1/2 lb. SR300: 4 scoops of 43 cc = 120 g; timer max 9.9 min. Sources describe fixed heat settings (390/455/490 F targets) and no temperature readout, so no readout is assumed; an owner-added probe is not supported by this entry. Discontinued/legacy model. Row count 12 is the owner's rule for the whole Fresh Roast SR series (10 min is about the longest anyone roasts on it, +2 buffer). Tier 2: SR300 has no temperature readout, so no start model or wizard. Retailer: variable fan, three fixed heat settings, timer to 9.9 min, a 3-minute cooling cycle. The 30-minute gap is the SR540 manual's rule, assumed for the family.

250 g (200 g for natural process, per Sweet Maria's). Manufacturer's roast chart runs 12 min (Light) to 23 min (Italian); timer 1-23 min; setpoint 374-482 F. One thermocouple; manual says the display shows roasting-chamber temperature, which reads well above actual bean temperature. Time 10:00-25:00, target temperature 167-428 F, display switchable F/C. External cooling tray. Tier 2: Manual: preheat until it beeps at 167 F, then add the beans; heater 0-100%, fan in five 25% steps, cooling tray. The machine cools itself if restarted too hot, so no fixed gap. First crack 12:30 comes from the manual's worked example (about 5:00 remaining in a 17:30 roast). The example was for the P-2K, assumed for this model. First-crack display temperature 385 F (the manual's colour chart: beans about 400 F at a display of about 385 F).

Nano 7: 120 g standard batch; 50-200 g with the optional Boost kit (the maximum allows for it). Roast Companion: probe touches the beans (reads 5-10 C above true bean-surface temperature); first crack about 205 C; roast usually ended 220-230 C; profile = temperature curve plus fan curve, ended by a 'roast level'. Typical roast under 10 min; cool-down 2-3 min. Tier 2: Roaster's Companion: no true preheat (the curve starts about 110 C at 60 s); roast level 0.1-5.9 ends the roast; first crack about 205 C; worked example: a 10-minute roast with first crack at 7:30 (development 20-25% of the roast, per Scott Rao); cool-down 2-3 min; roast again as soon as cool-down ends. The six-tier DTR table is the app's published one, inferred.

M3: handbook batch 250-300 g (cooling bin handles about 300 g or less). Handbook: temperatures are in Celsius; ships with one analog thermometer, ports for bean (BT) and environment (ET) probes; BT reading varies with probe placement and batch size; overall roast 11-22 min; first crack about 205 C. First crack 12:00 inferred as the middle of the handbook's 8-16 minute drying-plus-ramp range.
